fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E (Sept-2027 NTM adj. EPS ~$10.54 x 25x = ~$263.5, a multiple now cross-checked against peers ETN 26.8x / NVT 24.8x FY27) and 40% DCF valued at Sept 2027 (WACC 10%, terminal growth 4%, op margin to 27% by 2030; horizon net cash cut to ~+$0.3B after the $1.45B UIG payment, with UIG credited at ~75% of cost = ~$247/share). Blended ~$257 for Vertiv Holdings Co (NYSE: VRT).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EPS at Sept 2027 = 0.25 x FY27 $9.16 + 0.75 x FY28 $11.00 = $10.54; x 25x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: +20% on the $9.16 FY27 consensus. Management's May 2026 framework is 20-22% revenue CAGR (2025-30) with adj. op margin going from ~23.8% (FY26 guide) to 27%+ by 2030, which implies ~22-25% EPS growth; haircut to 20% because consensus FY27 revenue ($18.2B) already runs ahead of that CAGR path, and for Q2's execution slippage. Round 2: cross-checked against the ~$11.19 aggregator FY28 consensus cited by the supervisor (secondary, not independently verified); I keep $11.00 because FY27 consensus ($9.16, Alpha Vantage re-pulled 2026-09-29) is unchanged and the aggregator figure is not from a primary feed. UIG is guided 'accretive to adjusted EPS in the first year' (8-K 2026-09-02) but no EBITDA base is disclosed, so I add nothing for it.

Stock now at ~26.6x FY27 consensus ($244/$9.16). Near the 52-week high ($380) it traded at ~41-43x the FY27 EPS estimates of the time (~$8.8 60-90 days ago). With growth slowing from ~60% EPS growth (FY26) to ~20% (FY28), I apply a slight discount to today's multiple rather than a re-rating either way. Round 2: the supervisor's peer check (ETN 26.8x, NVT 24.8x FY27; Schneider ~26-30x) shows VRT is not at a premium, which supports 25x rather than a peer-convergence de-rating; I do not go above 25x because orders have not been disclosed since Q4 2025 and the Texas permit freeze (source 15) adds order-timing risk.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue FY27 $18.2B, then +18%/15%/12%/10%/9%/8%/7%/6% to 2035 ($40.7B); adj. op margin 25% (27) -> 26% (28) -> 26.5% (29) -> 27% (2030+); tax 21%; FCF = 90% of NOPAT; WACC 10%; terminal growth 4%; valued at Sept 2027; horizon net cash ~+$0.3B plus UIG credited at ~$1.1B (75% of $1.45B cost) = ~$1.4B non-operating add (was $2.5B); 395M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Starts slightly below management's 20-22% 5-year revenue CAGR target and data-center TAM growth of 18-20%, then fades toward nominal GDP-plus as the AI build-out matures.
FY26 guide is 23.3-24.3% and Q2 came in at 22.6%. The 2030 target is 27%+ (raised from 25%+). I assume the target is reached with no further upside.

Management targets 95-100% FCF conversion and 3-4% capex/sales, but the 10-Q shows inventories up $1.05B in 1H26 ($1.46B to $2.52B) that was funded by a $1.82B deferred-revenue build. I haircut conversion because that customer-prepayment tailwind should reverse as growth slows. Round 2: the supervisor confirmed from the 10-Q that H1 adj. FCF ($1.58B) was less than the +$1.82B deferred-revenue build, so ex-deposits H1 FCF was negative; my 90% conversion on NOPAT (not a grown $2.5B FCF base) already avoids capitalizing deposits, so I keep it.

The balance sheet is near net-cash (cash $2.81B + ST inv. $0.30B vs debt $2.94B at 6/30/26), so WACC is roughly cost of equity. High beta and 60%+ realized vol argue for ~10%. Terminal growth of 4% reflects secular data-center demand.

inputs_detail.input: Net cash at Sept 2027 (plus UIG credit)
inputs_detail.value: ~+$0.3B net cash, plus ~$1.1B credit for UIG = ~$1.4B total add-back (round 1: $2.5B)
inputs_detail.derivation: +$0.17B net cash at 6/30/26 (10-Q: cash $2.81B + ST inv $0.30B - debt $2.94B), + implied H2 2026 adj. FCF $0.8-1.0B (FY guide $2.4-2.6B less H1 $1.58B), - $1.45B UIG cash at a Q4 2026 close, - King Environmental (Q4 2026 close, price undisclosed), - $0.235B accrued contingent consideration, - dividends ($0.0625/qtr x ~393M = ~$0.1B/yr), + ~9 months of 2027 FCF ($1-2B, lower if deposits unwind), - early UIG earnout (up to $1.15B over 12-24 months, EBITDA-contingent) => ~+$0.3B central (range -$0.5B to +$1.2B). Unlike the supervisor, I do not simply drop the cash: the $1.45B buys an earning business (~13x 2027 EBITDA, i.e. ~$110M EBITDA) that my consensus-based revenue path may not fully include, so I credit UIG at ~75% of cost to allow for integration/earnout risk and possible overlap with consensus. Net change vs round 1: -$1.1B, about -$2.8/share.
~$0.17B net cash at 6/30/26 + ~$2.5B+ annual adj. FCF, less dividends, bolt-on M&A (5 deals since Aug 2025, ~$1.5B) and up to ~$0.25B in PurgeRite/other earnouts.

bear.story: AI capex digestion: hyperscaler FCF strain leads to project push-outs. The Texas TCEQ permit halt (from 2026-09-21, covering islanded/behind-the-meter sites too) runs past the mid-December ERCOT audit and copycat state actions follow. Vertiv's multiphase coordination problems recur, H2 2026 misses the guide, deferred revenue ($3.63B) unwinds and FCF turns weak as deposits reverse. FY28 EPS ~$8.5 at ~16-17x, near the 52-week low.

base.story: Q3/Q4 2026 roughly meet guide (Q3 $3.65-3.85B, EPS $1.77-1.83; consensus sits at $1.83), FY26 ~$6.70-6.73 EPS. UIG and King close in Q4 2026. Texas permitting resumes after the audits with delays but no lost orders. 2027 guidance near consensus (~$18.2B revenue, ~$9.2 EPS). The stock trades at ~25x NTM EPS of ~$10.5, in line with ETN/NVT.

bull.story: Execution issues clear; OneCore/SmartRun and UIG-led early engagement (behind-the-meter power design) pull through more content per MW; 2027 guide beats ($10+ EPS) and margins reach 26%+ early. 800V DC sidecars ramp in H2 2027. Multiple re-rates to ~32x FY28 EPS of ~$13, above the prior $380 high.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$165 the stock would trade at ~18x FY27 consensus ($9.16) and ~15.7x my Sept-2027 NTM EPS ($10.54), far below ETN (26.8x) and NVT (24.8x) FY27, so it would signal falling earnings rather than a timing slip or an ordinary de-rating. I keep $165 rather than the supervisor's $155 because the peer check shows no premium to unwind, so a move to high-teens multiples needs an earnings problem, and the 66% vol range around the Q3 print is already covered above that level. Confirming evidence: deferred revenue falling from $3.63B without a revenue step-up, a second revenue miss framed as 'timing', FY27 guidance below ~$8.5 EPS, a margin guide cut, or the Texas permit halt extending well past the mid-December ERCOT audit and spreading to other states.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. Primary documents still show accelerating fundamentals: Q2 2026 sales $3.27B (+24%), adj. EPS $1.52 (+60%), FY26 guide $14.0B / $6.70 / $2.4-2.6B FCF, 2030 targets of 20-22% revenue CAGR and 27%+ margin; FY27 consensus re-pulled on 2026-09-29 is $9.16 (up from $8.80 in 90 days), FY26 $6.73, Q3 $1.83. The supervisor's findings changed three things. (1) Net cash: I had +$2.5B at the horizon; after the $1.45B UIG payment (8-K 2026-09-02), King (8-K 2026-09-24), contingent consideration, dividends ($0.0625/qtr per the June 8-K) and a deposit-dependent FCF path, ~+$0.3B is more realistic. I credit UIG at ~75% of cost since the cash buys an earning asset, so the DCF falls $250 -> $247 (a smaller cut than the supervisor's ~$4/share, and I say why). (2) Texas: I verified the freeze in primary form (Governor's release of 2026-09-21) and a law-firm alert: it halts all data-center permits, including islanded/behind-the-meter sites, until ERCOT (mid-Dec 2026) and TWDB audits finish, with a TCEQ report due 2026-10-19. That argues for a fatter left-middle, so I moved 3 points from base/bull into bear (bear 27%/base 49%/bull 24%) and lowered P(>=K) by ~1-1.5 points for K = 146-244. (3) Peer multiples (ETN 26.8x, NVT 24.8x FY27) confirm that VRT is not at a premium, supporting my 25x P/E leg unchanged at $263.5; I kept FY28 at $11.00 vs the ~$11.19 aggregator figure. Blended fair value is $257 (was $258). The ladder is a lognormal-like distribution with its median ~$254 and log-sigma ~0.55, a slightly fatter left-middle and near-unchanged tails; the scenario mean is ~$267 with right skew; P(>= spot $244) = 0.53. The Q3 date is late October (aggregators show Oct 28) and not yet confirmed by Vertiv. Round-2 research: 7 lookups (UIG, King and dividend 8-Ks, the Governor's release, the Bracewell alert, an earnings-calendar search, Alpha Vantage consensus). No option data and nothing under priors/ was used.
